locator.text: Display 36.1, p. 36, in the statement of Lemma 4.9

evidence: paper: T_\theta(r) = r^{-2}\int_r^{\infty} r'^2 R^{(0)}_\theta(r')\,dr', \qquad T_z(r) = r^{-1}\int_r^{\infty} r' R^{(0)}_z(r')\,dr',

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary:
Lean has a weaker form of it. Where the Lean states the display, the formulas agree. Angular half: terminalStress unfolds to backwardStress of leadingResidual, which is literally r^{-2}∫_r^∞ u^2 R(u) du. Axial half: axialBackwardStress is the same primitive in the variable s = r'^2/2 (ds = r' dr'), with integrand ∂_z of the canonical pressure, which is the axial residual of the terminal field where the meridional velocity vanishes. The left sides are the physical stress q^{-A-1/2}·(similarity stress), as in the paper.

What is missing is range. Both theorems carry hfull : 1/2 < log(X/switchRadius) + 1/5, which by TerminalCone.tailTime_clock is y > tailStart + 1/2, i.e. X > e^{1/2} X_tail. The right-hand residual is that of the terminal heat profile (normalization, outgoingTaper), which is the leading field's residual only on that range. The paper's display is printed for the stress of the whole leading field with no restriction on r. For r with X ≤ e^{1/2} X_tail (the switch interval and the inner extension) I found no declaration giving the stress as a backward integral of the actual field's residual. The constructed joined profile is tied to these formulas only for y ≥ terminalStart (LeadingStressWeights.nominal_terminal_stress). The generic TerminalStress.forward_eq_backward_iff covers the angular weight only and is never instantiated for the leading field (its only uses are in SlowFirstOrderEdge.lean).

A second, smaller narrowing: the Lean is about the compensated family's own forward stress (forwardTheta / forwardAxial under a CompensationWitness) and the one constructed profile, not about every leading field satisfying the paper's four hypotheses.

Everything the Lean states follows from the display. The paper's own source for the display, Lemma A.8 (p. 140), claims the backward representation only 'on y ≥ 1/2, where χ_K = 1', which is the Lean's range. The conclusions drawn from the display in Lemma 4.9 (T_0 = 0 for X ≥ X_b; the cone and (4.32) on e^{1/2}X_tail ≤ X < X_b) lie inside it, so severity is low.
